annotation.authors_or_issuer: Surendran, V.; Cruz, A.M.; Wagner, A.R.; Borenstein, J.; Arkin, R.C.; Chen, S.
key_provisions_or_claims: No single ethical framework captures human ethical decision-making; a robot architecture should use multiple frameworks.
Surveyed 100 US lay adults (folk morality) and philosophy-professor ethics experts on deception in pill-sorting and child game scenarios.
Experts often answered 'uncertain' when applying frameworks, especially Social Justice Theory (over 50%).
Scenario features may eventually determine which ethical framework a robot applies.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper reporting surveys of lay adults and ethics experts on deception in a pill-sorting (older adult care) and child game-playing scenario, to inform a robot ethics architecture that selects among multiple ethical frameworks. Finds substantial expert uncertainty across frameworks and explores folk reasoning.
annotation.title_clean: Informing a Robot Ethics Architecture Through Folk and Expert Morality
annotation.title_en: Informing a Robot Ethics Architecture Through Folk and Expert Morality
annotation.venue: ICRES 2022: 7th International Conference on Robot Ethics and Standards
